definition_in_source: Order revoked by the end of the following presidential term (binary); non-ceremonial in the main models
nearest_project_term: formal_disposition (instrument, date) with mechanism express_revocation, then a window computed from its date
relation: narrower: a time-windowed indicator of one formal act
where_definitions_differ: Project records one formal disposition per order with exact date and separates it from operative end (TC01, TC13); L&P collapse to a yes/no inside a 1-7 year window and ignore later revocations. No whole/partial split; no operative-effect information.

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if the order's function releases non-recoverable assets or personnel, physically moves or alters property, or designates assets or personnel for a purpose; coded from title (63%) or by hand (37%)
nearest_project_term: No field. Nearest: TC06 durable_status, TC07 spent_dispositive_act_convention, enduring_legal_consequence
relation: different axis (irreversibility of outcomes in the world; not legal effect)
where_definitions_differ: An order that sold land or paid a one-time raise is immutable for L&P but a spent dispositive act with no operative force under TC07 unless an independent continuing norm or status is shown (TC06). Temporary closings are immutable and ceremonial together. Coded from the title, not from the operative text; 'we cannot actually observe a policy's effects' (p. 353).

definition_in_source: Coded ceremonial: honorifics and awards, holiday closing of offices, renaming of facilities; no operational rule or codebook in the deposit
source_ref: article p. 354 and p. 352; SI-13 Table C.2
nearest_project_term: No field. Nearest: ever_operative_states hortatory_only; TC07 spent dispositive acts
where_definitions_differ: The project has no ceremonial class and decides effect clause by clause; a ceremonial order is not presumed to lack operative effect. L&P exclude these from the main models.

definition_in_source: Order deals with foreign policy (binary)
nearest_project_term: none (a topic tag)
where_definitions_differ: Not a legal-status concept; nearest source variable is Thrower fds (foreign, defense or national security).

definition_in_source: Year issued (calendar year; counts match the master register in 76 of 84 years 1937-2020)
nearest_project_term: date (exact signing date) in the register
where_definitions_differ: Year only; no EO number. Thrower's year is a president-coded year, not calendar year, for orders in January of inauguration years (106 orders differ from the register).

variable: war; election; inflation; admchg; endterm; trend37; issuing_divgov; opposing_next; next_term_divgov
definition_in_source: Political and economic covariates at the year or term level
nearest_project_term: none
where_definitions_differ: Controls for a regression; the project does not model revocation timing. SI-3 reports L&P corrected war, election-day and revoking-president coding relative to Thrower.

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if the order is revoked (any revocation), 0 otherwise
nearest_project_term: formal_disposition with mechanism express_revocation
relation: narrower in time, broader in scope
where_definitions_differ: Formal label from the Executive Orders Disposition Tables; whole and partial revocation are separate flags; 20 revocations missing and 1 false (SI-2). Project: a formal revocation alone never shows operative end (TC01, TC13, ESTIMAND.md).

definition_in_source: Year in which the order is revoked
nearest_project_term: formal_disposition.date; whole_order_end is the latest clause first end, a different date
where_definitions_differ: Year not date; the formal act's date, not the end of operation. Project's formal_revocation_after_earlier_cessation is derived when the disposition postdates an established end.

definition_in_source: Header in the CSV says revoked by other than an executive order; the PDF codebook lists revokedbyeo12553 (revoked by EO 12553); 140 rows flagged in the CSV, 98.6% of them revoked; only 1 of 377 orders revoked in 1986 is flagged
nearest_project_term: first_cause_type (legislative, judicial, regulatory) and mechanism (statutory_termination, judicial_invalidation, regulatory_action)
relation: unresolved: the name and the description disagree
where_definitions_differ: I could not tell which meaning the column carries; ask Thrower (eo_original_list.do does not mention it). The CSV does not identify which orders EO 12553 revoked.

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if the order is superseded; year
nearest_project_term: mechanism express_supersession or implied_supersession; formal_disposition
relation: equivalent in kind, narrower in coverage
where_definitions_differ: 471 rows superseded, 45 of them also revoked. SI-2: the disposition tables use supersession and revocation interchangeably; L&P drop it from the outcome. Project counts any formal revocation, supersession or rescission as formal disposition (ESTIMAND.md) but keeps the mechanism.

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if the order is partially revoked
nearest_project_term: clause-level later_events with scope_id; TC02 demand_driven_episode
where_definitions_differ: Project works clause by clause and a partial change does not support whole closure (frozen codebook, inference exceptions). 118 rows flagged; whether they count in revoked is not stated.

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if substantively amended; year
nearest_project_term: mechanism amendment; first_cause_type later_amendment_imposed_condition; TC09 incorporated_amendment
where_definitions_differ: Amendment is an event on a clause, not an end of the order. Thrower's amended flag is order-level and substantive only.

definition_in_source: Revocation types: by rejection of authority, transferring authority, abolishing an agency, amending a related policy, rejecting authority while amending an unrelated area
nearest_project_term: mechanism (body_abolished, authority_repealed_or_lapsed, express_revocation) plus actor
where_definitions_differ: Classifies the revoking order's purpose; the project classifies how the first end occurred and who caused it (first_cause_type), and keeps cleanup dates apart (TC13).

definition_in_source: Coded 1 if the order is related to ceremonial purposes
nearest_project_term: none
where_definitions_differ: Counts per calendar year equal L&P's ceremonial counts in every year 1937-2013 (README.md). Row-level agreement confirmed only in years where the alignment test passes.

variable: fds; civilservice; publicland; economy; committee; civilrights; intelligence; nationalsecurity; foreignservice; militaryoperations; governmentcontracting; temporaryandemergencyfunctions
definition_in_source: Topic dummies
nearest_project_term: none
where_definitions_differ: Subject tags. temporaryandemergencyfunctions is the closest to an order that may end under its own terms (under_original_terms), but it is a topic, not a finding.

definition_in_source: Executive order number as designated by the Federal Register; year issued
nearest_project_term: instrument_id (EO:number, suffix), date
where_definitions_differ: Includes lettered orders such as 7677-A as separate rows (suffix). All 6,158 Thrower rows join to the register by number and suffix.

definition_in_source: Revocation recorded in disposition tables; orders may be 'alive' on paper though spent
nearest_project_term: formal validity (unrevoked on the books) as a separate column
where_definitions_differ: Project's headline is operative force at 2026-10-14, not formal validity. L&P have no operative-force measure.

definition_in_source: Disposition-table term treated as interchangeable with revocation; 37 cases excluded from Thrower's data
nearest_project_term: mechanism other with mechanism_note, or express_revocation
where_definitions_differ: The codebook's mechanism list has no 'nullified'; a case would need mechanism_note (required for other).

definition_in_source: Orders revoked decades later, as in EO 12553 (1986), seen as spent (SI-3)
nearest_project_term: TC13 cleanup_dates; formal_revocation_after_earlier_cessation; the re-tagged not_later_than claims
where_definitions_differ: L&P assert it for EO 12553 without a count; the project defines it as a derived field requiring an evidenced earlier end, and treats a shared revocation date as a bound until then.

definition_in_source: yes, no, indeterminate: whether any clause still had operative effect at the 2026-10-14 cutoff (rollup rule TC03)
nearest_project_term: none in L&P or Thrower
where_definitions_differ: Neither prior dataset records operative force or any end other than a formal act.

definition_in_source: How the first end occurred (under_original_terms, later_presidential, legislative, judicial, completion_of_task, never_activated, unresolved); whole_order_end is the latest clause first end
nearest_project_term: none in L&P or Thrower
where_definitions_differ: Prior data cannot show an order ended before its formal revocation; they record one formal event.
